podcast.body: This song was TLC's number one smash hit from the spring of 1999, characterized by its "sleek, chiming, percolating hip-hop sound." It served as a direct "template" for the sound Pink adopted on her debut album, and Pink's first hit, "There You Go," was crafted by the same producer and songwriters, Kevin "She'kspere" Briggs and Kandi Burruss, who worked on "No Scrubs." "No scrubs, TLC's number one smash from the spring of 1999, with its sleek, chiming, percolating hip-hop sound. Was a template for what Pink did on her debut album."

podcast.body: This song was one of two Hot 100 number ones from their "FanMail" album. It advocated for self-reliant women unimpressed with "shiftless men," flying the flag for female empowerment in 1999, similar to Destiny's Child's "Bills, Bills, Bills." "The aforementioned No Scrubs. Which, like Destiny's Bill's Bill's Bill's, flew the flag in 1999 for self-reliant women unimpressed with shiftless men."
